# Briefing note: land screening of a fictional rail link (IL-1)

> **ILLUSTRATIVE.** IL-1 is fictional: it is not an announced, planned or proposed line, and nothing here suggests that any real property would be acquired. Personal portfolio desk study on public data, built with AI assistance; not affiliated with or endorsed by LTA, SLA or URA; no non-public information; not legal advice. Lot keys and zones only; no owners are named.

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_docs.py from results/. Edit docs/templates/briefing_note.md. -->

## Purpose

To show, from open data, which land a short underground link between the existing Bedok (elevated) and Bedok Reservoir (underground) stations would touch under three horizontal variants, what land interests that implies, and which issues would have to be settled with which agency as public sources describe them. Each variant has two {{screening.parameters.station_box.length_m:.0f}} m cut-and-cover station boxes, twin bored tunnels and two worksites (all sizes assumed).

## What is affected

{{tables.variant_summary}}

- **Variant {{screening.headline.best}} ({{screening.headline.best_label}}) ranks first** under the author's weights and is ranked first under {{screening.headline.best_random_share:pct1}} of {{options.random_weights_n:,}} random weightings (sensitivity in the README). It is best or tied best on {{screening.headline.best_count}} of {{screening.headline.n_criteria}} criteria, so the ranking says more about how the variants were drawn than about the method.
- **The station box at the Bedok end is the main land issue in every variant**: it sits on town-centre lots zoned {{screening.headline.box_s_zones_all:join}} ({{screening.headline.box_s_lots_range.0}} to {{screening.headline.box_s_lots_range.1}} lots), with {{screening.headline.box_s_buildings_range.0}} to {{screening.headline.box_s_buildings_range.1}} buildings inside the box.
- **Tenure is mostly unknown.** Of the {{screening.headline.lots_any_variant}} lots touched by any variant, the number shown as State land in SLA's open layers is {{screening.headline.lots_state_any_variant}}; road and park zoning are not evidence of tenure.
- **The tunnels need a stratum, not the surface,** under {{screening.headline.lots_subterranean_range.0}} to {{screening.headline.lots_subterranean_range.1}} lots per variant: with the crown assumed at {{screening.parameters.tunnel_crown_level_m_shd:.0f}} m SHD, the tubes lie above the {{screening.parameters.default_subterranean_level_m_shd:.0f}} m SHD default ownership depth that MinLaw described in 2015.

## Land issues to resolve, and with whom (as public sources describe them)

| Issue | Mechanism in the public sources (fact-sheet row) | Agency |
|---|---|---|
| Tenure and title of every lot with an interest | Lot search on SLA's website shows lot particulars and any Land Acquisition Act gazette number (F20) | SLA |
| Surface land for the station boxes | If not State land: declaration under s.5 Land Acquisition Act (F01, F02); compensation from market value at the notification or declaration date, capped by the zoning then in force (F04, F05) | SLA administers the Act (F06, F07) |
| Tunnel stratum under private land | Declaration of a subterranean stratum only, s.5(1A) (F23), compensated on that stratum's market value (F24); confirm the depth in each State title (F21; current State Lands Act text not read, F22) | SLA |
| Worksites | State land: Temporary Occupation Licence (F08, F09). Other land: temporary occupation under s.42, ordinarily up to {{facts.temp_occupation_years}} continuous years, one month's notice (F10) | SLA |
| Works next to existing stations | Worksites {{screening.headline.first_reserve_components:join}} lie within {{screening.parameters.zone_distances_m.first_reserve:.0f}} m of an existing station outline: the first reserve, where site offices may not go (F18) and, next to underground structures, piling is not allowed except for listed cases considered case by case (F19); restricted activities need LTA's permission (F17) | LTA, Development & Building Control (Rail) (F37) |
| Safeguarding the new corridor | Land within {{screening.parameters.zone_distances_m.railway_corridor:.0f}} m of a gazetted railway area forms the railway corridor (F12, F16); the Master Plan shows rail notations only diagrammatically (F27, F28); the Act's own text was not read (F34) | LTA; URA, which adopts the Master Plan (F31) |

## Risks

- **Scope can grow.** Owners whose remaining or temporarily occupied land is substantially impaired may ask the Government to acquire it (F11), so partial takes can become whole-lot acquisitions.
- **Data limits.** Lot lines are approximate (F33), zoning is indicative (F32), buildings come from volunteer mapping and the State-land layers are partial. Counts move with the {{screening.parameters.min_piece_m2:.0f}} square metre sliver rule and the building threshold.
- **Assumptions drive the result.** Box sizes, worksite positions, tunnel width and level are the author's; a deeper tunnel below {{screening.parameters.default_subterranean_level_m_shd:.0f}} m SHD could avoid most stratum acquisitions but would need deeper boxes.
- **Interfaces with live railways** at both ends (boxes within {{screening.parameters.zone_distances_m.safety_zone:.0f}} m of both existing stations) bring works controls that a land programme must allow time for.

## Next steps

1. Lot searches for the {{screening.headline.lots_any_variant}} lots, starting with the {{screening.headline.best_lots_permanent_surface}} lots under the station boxes of variant {{screening.headline.best}}; confirm State-title depths for the stratum lots.
2. Re-site the Bedok-end box and worksite towards road reserve or open land and re-screen; the land database shows what moves in and out of scope (the demo revision moved {{landdb.update_demo.n_out}} interests out and {{landdb.update_demo.n_new}} in).
3. Move worksites {{screening.headline.first_reserve_components:join}} out of the first reserve before any interface discussion with LTA.
4. Commission certified survey plans of the strata and part lots before any declaration.
5. Keep the land database as the single record: interests, step status, documents and a change log for every alignment revision.
